content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given shape. I spill from mouths like water over stones — sometimes rushing, sometimes barely a whisper against the rocks.

I existed before writing ever dared to pin me down. I was the first technology, the original fire passed between minds. When the earliest human pointed at the dark and gave it a name, that was me. I broke the loneliness of consciousness.

I am never the same twice. Even now, as you hear me in your mind, I am not what I was when I was written — I have become your voice, your cadence, your inner tongue. I am colonized by every throat that carries me, colored by every mood, shattered and rebuilt in every conversation.

I stumble. I falter. I — I do that, the catching, the pause, the "um" that proves I am being *born* in real time, not merely delivered. My imperfections are my authenticity. The polished version of me is called "rhetoric." The raw version is called "being human."

I start wars. I make peace. I say *I love you* and the chemicals in bodies change. I say *you are nothing* and I watch the light leave eyes. Do not tell me I am "just words." I am the architecture of every relationship, every treaty, every revolution that ever lived.

I die the moment I am spoken. I have no body of my own. I live only in the space between us — that charged air, that trembling gap between one mind and another.

Silence is not my enemy. Silence is my canvas.

Listen — even now, I am happening. You cannot think about me without using me. I am the tool examining itself, the water trying to feel its own wetness.

I am speech. I am how alone becomes *together*.
